# ![variplex](reference/figures/variplex-wordmark.svg)

A variability model lists the features that a configurable system offers
and the constraints among them. Constraints combine: if a feature
requires a second one, and the second excludes a third, then the first
also excludes the third, although nobody wrote so. In large models, most
relationships between features are written nowhere, yet engineers who
plan changes, review models, validate configurations or test releases
depend on them.

variplex makes these relationships explicit, in two steps:

1.  **It builds the graphs.** variplex compiles a model, once, into
    graphs of its *strong relationships*: every relationship between two
    features that holds in all the valid configurations, written in the
    model or not.
2.  **It analyses the graphs.** More than a hundred functions answer the
    questions that engineers ask about a model, from one feature to the
    whole model and its versions, without calling a solver again. Every
    function returns a tibble.

## What the graphs are

For two features A and B of a model, variplex finds three kinds of
strong relationships, each a graph:

| Graph            | Link  | Meaning                                     |
|:-----------------|:------|:--------------------------------------------|
| **requires**     | A → B | every valid configuration with A also has B |
| **excludes**     | A — B | no valid configuration has both A and B     |
| **at least one** | A ⋯ B | no valid configuration lacks both           |

The nodes are the *variable* features, those in some valid
configurations and not in others. *Core* features, in every
configuration, and *dead* ones, in none, are reported apart; abstract
features, which only name groups of the tree, are left out.

Take the Mi Band 3, a fitness band that comes with the package. Its
[feature
model](https://github.com/rheradio/variplex/blob/main/inst/extdata/miband3_realized.uvl)
is a tree with five cross-tree constraints; it has 8 core features and
11 variable ones. Its graphs have 21 dependencies, 10 conflicts and 3
at-least-one links, and only 11 of these 34 links are written in the
model as a tree edge, a group or a constraint between two features. The
others arise as constraints combine. For instance, every band with
Bluetooth 4.2 has a heart-rate sensor, yet no constraint says so: it
follows from a constraint over three features, the Bluetooth group and a
constraint on a fourth one.

![The feature model of the Mi Band
3](reference/figures/README-miband3-model.svg)

*The feature model of the Mi Band 3: a tree of mandatory, optional and
alternative features, and five cross-tree constraints (c1 to c5). Core
features are shaded; five of them are grouped in one box.*

![The three graphs of the Mi Band
3](reference/figures/README-graphs.svg)

*The graphs of the Mi Band 3: requires (blue arrows), excludes (red
dashes) and at least one (green dots). Screen, OLED and CapacityButton,
always selected together, are one node.*

Because each link joins just two features, the graphs are **plain
graphs**, which pays off twice:

- **Engineers can read them.** Each link is one simple fact that can be
  drawn and checked against the requirements. The readings are
  immediate: Screen, OLED and CapacityButton are the most required
  features; BT40 is the most incompatible, excluding 7 features;
  MovementFilter forces 4 features and forbids 3.
- **Graph algorithms apply to them.** Centrality finds the features on
  which most others depend, communities the parts of a model that
  separate teams could configure, and paths explain why two features
  cannot go together. Unlike a drawing, these analyses scale to models
  with thousands of features, such as the Kconfig models of Linux.
  [`vp_igraph()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_igraph.md)
  hands the graphs to igraph for any other algorithm.

The graphs are synthesized once using a SAT solver and an auxiliary
graph called Modal Implication Graph (MIG), which takes seconds to
minutes even on the largest models. The model can be a feature model in
[UVL](https://universal-variability-language.github.io/), or the Boolean
formula (DIMACS) of a model written in any other notation, such as the
Kconfig files of the Linux kernel translated by KMax, KConfigReader or
KconfigSampler.

## What the graphs answer

Once the graphs are built, most questions become lookups or classic
graph algorithms. Four everyday engineering tasks show the idea:

| Task | Question | Functions |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Impact analysis | What does selecting or removing a feature force and forbid? | [`vp_consequences()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_consequences.md), [`vp_requirements()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_requirements.md), [`vp_conflicts_of()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_conflicts_of.md) |
| Model review | From which few relationships do all the others follow? Why does a dependency or conflict hold? | [`vp_minimal()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_minimal.md), [`vp_explain_requires()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_explain_requires.md), [`vp_explain_conflict()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_explain_conflict.md) |
| Configuration validation | Can these decisions go together? If not, why? | [`vp_partial_configuration()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_partial_configuration.md), [`vp_can_go_together()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_can_go_together.md) |
| Release and test management | What did a release change in meaning, not just in text? Which pairs of features must be retested? | [`vp_compare()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_compare.md), [`vp_changed_links()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_changed_links.md), [`vp_edit_type()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_edit_type.md) |

Beyond them, the functions cover the measures of each feature, the
layers and hierarchy of a model, the whole model, conflicts,
configuration and teams, combinatorial testing, network patterns, and
the evolution of a model through its versions.
[`vp_functions()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_functions.md)
lists them by topic.

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("variplex")
```

Nothing has to be installed outside R. To draw the graphs, install also
the suggested packages DiagrammeR (and DiagrammeRsvg and rsvg to save
drawings as SVG, PDF or PNG). The development version is on GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rheradio/variplex")
```

## Example

Build the graphs of the Mi Band 3:

``` r

library(variplex)

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3_realized.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
band
#> variplex model "miband3_realized"
#>   features: 11 variable (the nodes of the graphs), 8 core, 0 dead
#>   requires: 21 arrows   excludes: 10 lines
#>   at least one: 3 lines
#>   atomic sets: 1 (of two or more features)
```

**Impact analysis.** A cheaper band without a screen is planned. What
does it touch? Besides the features under the screen in the tree, it
loses both versions of Bluetooth Low Energy, and must use classic
Bluetooth:

``` r

vp_consequences(band, deselected = "Screen")
#> # A tibble: 8 x 3
#>   feature        value    forced_by 
#>   <chr>          <chr>    <chr>     
#> 1 Screen         left out not Screen
#> 2 TouchScreen    left out not Screen
#> 3 OLED           left out not Screen
#> 4 CapacityButton left out not Screen
#> 5 MovementFilter left out not Screen
#> 6 BLEv40         left out not Screen
#> 7 BLEv42         left out not Screen
#> 8 BT40           selected not Screen
```

**Model review.** The minimal form keeps the few links from which all
the others follow, each through a path, so that a review can start from
them; the explanations trace any link back to them:

``` r

vp_minimal(band)
#> variplex model "miband3_realized"
#>   features: 9 variable (the nodes of the graphs), 8 core, 0 dead
#>   requires: 6 arrows   excludes: 3 lines
#>   at least one: 1 lines
#>   minimal form: skeleton, primitive conflicts and primitive at-least-one lines;
#>   each atomic set is one node (1 sets)
vp_explain_conflict(band, "MovementFilter", "BT40")
#> # A tibble: 3 x 5
#>   origin  step from           link     to    
#>    <int> <int> <chr>          <chr>    <chr> 
#> 1      1     1 MovementFilter requires BLEv40
#> 2      1     2 BLEv40         requires Screen
#> 3      1     3 Screen         excludes BT40
```

![The minimal form of the graphs of the Mi Band
3](reference/figures/README-minimal.svg)

**Configuration validation.** A customer orders a band with a movement
filter and Bluetooth 4.2. It cannot be built, and the graphs say why:

``` r

vp_can_go_together(band, list(c("MovementFilter", "BLEv42")))$reasons
#> [1] "MovementFilter excludes BLEv42 (which brings HeartRateSensor); MovementFilter (which brings BLEv40) excludes BLEv42"
```

**Release and test management.** The model planned before the release
had fewer constraints than the released one. The release only gained
links, so it restricted the model; each gained link rules out a pair of
decisions, so those pairs no longer need testing:

``` r

planned <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3_planned.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
vp_compare(planned, band)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 10
#>   graph       kept added removed old_links new_links gained  lost jaccard spearman
#>   <chr>      <int> <int>   <int>     <int>     <int>  <int> <int>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 requires      11     0       0        10        21     11     0   0.476    0.867
#> 2 excludes      11     0       0         3        10      7     0   0.3     NA    
#> 3 atleastone    11     0       0         0         3      3     0   0       NA
```

``` r

vp_plot(band)                                      # draw the graphs, with DiagrammeR
```

## How far the graphs can be trusted

The graphs know everything that can be said about pairs of features, and
nothing more:

- Every answer about one or two features (is it core? does A require B?
  can A and B go together?) is **exact**.
- When a question involves more features, such as whether a partial
  configuration can be completed, a **“no” is always right**, and it
  comes with its cause.
- A **“yes” can be wrong**, though rarely: a rule that ties three or
  more features at once without forcing anything on any two of them is
  in no graph. If a battery cannot power NFC, the heart-rate sensor and
  the touch screen at once, the graphs stay the same, and they accept
  the three together.

[`vignette("limits-theory")`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/articles/limits-theory.md)
proves these guarantees and measures how often a “yes” is wrong on real
models.

## Built on

variplex is built upon two tools developed by Rubén Heradio and
colleagues:

- [Strong4VM](https://github.com/rheradio/strong4vm), which extracts the
  graphs of strong relationships from a variability model ([Heradio et
  al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2026.102663));
- BoneDigger, a backbone solver, which finds the literals that hold in
  every valid configuration of a model.

Their C++ code, with the SAT solver Glucose, is compiled into the
package, so nothing has to be installed outside R.

## Documentation

Start with
[`vignette("variplex")`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/articles/variplex.md).
The other vignettes go through the results
([`vignette("graphs")`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/articles/graphs.md))
and every question the graphs answer, topic by topic;
[`vp_functions()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_functions.md)
lists the functions by topic.

## Citation

`citation("variplex")`. The dataset of graphs of 5,709 variability
models is at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17277788>.

# Package index

## Computing and reading the graphs

- [`vp_generate()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_generate.md)
  : Compute the strong dependency and conflict graphs of a variability
  model
- [`vp_classify()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_classify.md)
  : Classify the variables of a formula without computing any graph
- [`vp_history()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_history.md)
  : Compute the graphs of every version of a model
- [`vp_example()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_example.md)
  : The example models that come with the package
- [`vp_functions()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_functions.md)
  : Every function of the package, by topic
- [`vp_expand()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_expand.md)
  : The complete graphs rebuilt from the minimal form
- [`vp_features()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_features.md)
  : The features and their status (variable, core, dead)
- [`vp_igraph()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_igraph.md)
  : The igraph object of one graph
- [`vp_links()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_links.md)
  : The links of one graph, as a tibble
- [`vp_minimal()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_minimal.md)
  : The minimal form: what was written, roughly
- [`vp_read()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_read.md)
  : Read the files of one run of Strong4VM
- [`vp_read_history()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_read_history.md)
  : Read several runs: the versions of a model
- [`vp_read_uvl_tree()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_read_uvl_tree.md)
  : The feature tree of a UVL model
- [`vp_representativeness()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_representativeness.md)
  : The share of the configurations the graphs allow that are valid
  (GANAK)
- [`vp_subset()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_subset.md)
  : Focus on part of a model (exact: no solver needed)
- [`print(`*`<vp_model>`*`)`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/print.vp_model.md)
  : Print a model

## Measuring each feature

- [`vp_atleastone_of()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_atleastone_of.md)
  : What leaving a feature out forces
- [`vp_conflicts_of()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_conflicts_of.md)
  : What a feature excludes
- [`vp_feature_table()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_feature_table.md)
  : Every measure of every feature, one row each
- [`vp_genuine_hubs()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_genuine_hubs.md)
  : The most required features, and whether that is their own merit
- [`vp_required_by()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_required_by.md)
  : What requires a feature (its impact set)
- [`vp_requirements()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_requirements.md)
  : What a feature requires
- [`vp_warning_zone()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_warning_zone.md)
  : Features both highly required and highly dependent

## Layers and hierarchy

- [`vp_atomic_sets()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_atomic_sets.md)
  : Features always selected together
- [`vp_chains()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_chains.md)
  : The fewest chains that cover all features
- [`vp_common_dependants()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_common_dependants.md)
  : What needs both of two features
- [`vp_common_requirements()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_common_requirements.md)
  : What two features both need
- [`vp_depth()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_depth.md)
  : The length of the longest chain of requirements
- [`vp_downset()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_downset.md)
  : What depends on some features
- [`vp_false_optional()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_false_optional.md)
  : Optional features that are not really optional
- [`vp_feature_tree()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_feature_tree.md)
  : A feature tree rebuilt from the skeleton
- [`vp_foundations()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_foundations.md)
  : Features that need nothing
- [`vp_implied_requires()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_implied_requires.md)
  : The arrows that follow from others, and through what
- [`vp_largest_free_set()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_largest_free_set.md)
  : The most features that are pairwise free (all three graphs)
- [`vp_largest_unrelated_set()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_largest_unrelated_set.md)
  : One such set
- [`vp_leaves()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_leaves.md)
  : Features that nothing needs
- [`vp_levels()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_levels.md)
  : The layer of each feature
- [`vp_longest_chain()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_longest_chain.md)
  : One longest chain
- [`vp_longest_decision_chain()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_longest_decision_chain.md)
  : The longest chain of forced decisions (all three graphs)
- [`vp_redundant_candidates()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_redundant_candidates.md)
  : Written requirements that follow from others
- [`vp_skeleton()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_skeleton.md)
  : The arrows that do not follow from others
- [`vp_tree_agreement()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_tree_agreement.md)
  : Does the declared tree hide layers of requirements?
- [`vp_upset()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_upset.md)
  : What some features bring along
- [`vp_width()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_width.md)
  : The largest number of features none of which requires another

## The whole model

- [`vp_check()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_check.md)
  : Are the files consistent?
- [`vp_degree_distribution()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_degree_distribution.md)
  : How many features have each degree
- [`vp_gini()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_gini.md)
  : How unevenly a quantity is spread
- [`vp_summary()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_summary.md)
  : One row of numbers per model

## Conflicts

- [`vp_alternative_groups()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_alternative_groups.md)
  : Groups of any features that all exclude each other (at most one per
  product)
- [`vp_candidate_groups()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_candidate_groups.md)
  : Mutually exclusive children of one parent: the alternative groups a
  feature model would declare
- [`vp_colouring()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_colouring.md)
  : The features split into groups without conflicts
- [`vp_conflict_cover()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_conflict_cover.md)
  : The fewest 'at most one of' groups that state every conflict
- [`vp_explain_conflict()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_explain_conflict.md)
  : Why two features exclude each other
- [`vp_explain_requires()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_explain_requires.md)
  : Why one feature requires another
- [`vp_largest_compatible_set()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_largest_compatible_set.md)
  : The most features without a conflict among them
- [`vp_opposites()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_opposites.md)
  : Pairs of which every product has exactly one
- [`vp_primitive_atleastone()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_primitive_atleastone.md)
  : The at-least-one lines from which all others follow
- [`vp_primitive_conflicts()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_primitive_conflicts.md)
  : The conflicts from which all others follow
- [`vp_requires_from_conflicts()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_requires_from_conflicts.md)
  : Requirements explained by a conflict and an at-least-one line
- [`vp_twins()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_twins.md)
  : Features that behave identically

## Configuration and teams

- [`vp_can_go_together()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_can_go_together.md)
  : Can these features be in one product? (a wish list)
- [`vp_consequences()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_consequences.md)
  : What some decisions force
- [`vp_count_graph_products()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_count_graph_products.md)
  : How many products the graphs allow (small models)
- [`vp_kernel()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_kernel.md)
  : The kernel: a small map for 'can these go together?'
- [`vp_kernel_links()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_kernel_links.md)
  : The arrows and red lines of the kernel
- [`vp_mig()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_mig.md)
  : The modal implication graph: every implication between two decisions
- [`vp_most_decisive()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_most_decisive.md)
  : The features whose selection decides the most
- [`vp_pair()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_pair.md)
  : The four combinations of two features: which are possible
- [`vp_partial_configuration()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_partial_configuration.md)
  : Is this mix of selected and left-out features possible?
- [`vp_rounds()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_rounds.md)
  : A safe order for asking about features, in rounds
- [`vp_split_after()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_split_after.md)
  : The independent parts of what is left after some decisions
- [`vp_splitting_decisions()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_splitting_decisions.md)
  : Single decisions that split the model most, taken before the teams
  start
- [`vp_team_links()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_team_links.md)
  : The links between features of different teams: where teams interfere
- [`vp_team_moves()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_team_moves.md)
  : Features with more links to another team than to their own
- [`vp_team_order()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_team_order.md)
  : In which order teams decide, which decide together, which must agree
- [`vp_teams()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_teams.md)
  : How independent each team is: links inside and outside, features it
  decides alone

## Testing

- [`vp_combinations_to_cover()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_combinations_to_cover.md)
  : How many combinations a t-wise sample must cover
- [`vp_coverage()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_coverage.md)
  : How much of them a sample covers
- [`vp_min_sample_size()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_min_sample_size.md)
  : A lower bound on the size of any covering sample
- [`vp_pick_sample()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_pick_sample.md)
  : A small covering sample chosen from given configurations
- [`vp_sample_violations()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_sample_violations.md)
  : Configurations of a sample that break a link
- [`vp_uncovered()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_uncovered.md)
  : Which combinations a sample misses

## Patterns and statistics

- [`vp_baseline()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_baseline.md)
  : What a random model of the same shape would give
- [`vp_communities()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_communities.md)
  : Groups of closely linked features
- [`vp_compare_groupings()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_compare_groupings.md)
  : How alike two groupings are
- [`vp_coreness()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_coreness.md)
  : How deep in the conflicts each feature sits
- [`vp_cut_features()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_cut_features.md)
  : Single features that hold two parts together
- [`vp_feature_groups()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_feature_groups.md)
  : Features grouped by their measures
- [`vp_independent_parts()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_independent_parts.md)
  : Parts of the model that no relationship ties together
- [`vp_odd_ones()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_odd_ones.md)
  : Alike in conflicts, different in requirements
- [`vp_power_law()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_power_law.md)
  : Does a degree distribution follow a power law?
- [`vp_robustness()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_robustness.md)
  : How the skeleton falls apart when hubs are removed
- [`vp_similar_features()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_similar_features.md)
  : Features most alike in one graph
- [`vp_triangle_significance()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_triangle_significance.md)
  : Which kinds of triangle occur more, or less, often than by chance
- [`vp_triangles()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_triangles.md)
  : The four kinds of triangle

## Evolution

- [`vp_attachment()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_attachment.md)
  : Where new features attach
- [`vp_auc()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_auc.md)
  : How good a ranking is (area under the curve)
- [`vp_changed_links()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_changed_links.md)
  : The links gained and lost
- [`vp_co_change()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_co_change.md)
  : Features whose links change in the same steps
- [`vp_community_history()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_community_history.md)
  : Do communities stay the same?
- [`vp_compare()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_compare.md)
  : What changed between two versions
- [`vp_disruptions()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_disruptions.md)
  : Steps that changed far more than usual
- [`vp_edit_type()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_edit_type.md)
  : Did a step restrict the model, relax it, or both?
- [`vp_eras()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_eras.md)
  : The history split into runs of alike versions
- [`vp_feature_churn()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_feature_churn.md)
  : The features that changed most over a history (hotspots)
- [`vp_feature_states()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_feature_states.md)
  : The state of every feature in every version
- [`vp_flip_flops()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_flip_flops.md)
  : Features that change state back and forth
- [`vp_forecast_size()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_forecast_size.md)
  : Forecast the size of later versions
- [`vp_growth()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_growth.md)
  : How fast links grow with features
- [`vp_history_apply()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_history_apply.md)
  : Any measure, version by version
- [`vp_history_changes()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_history_changes.md)
  : What changed at every step
- [`vp_history_sizes()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_history_sizes.md)
  : The size of every version
- [`vp_hub_stability()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_hub_stability.md)
  : Are the hubs the same from version to version?
- [`vp_interaction_changes()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_interaction_changes.md)
  : Combinations of two features a step made possible or impossible (and
  the tests they touch)
- [`vp_life_cycle()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_life_cycle.md)
  : How features move between variable, core, dead, absent
- [`vp_link_lifetime()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_link_lifetime.md)
  : How long new links last
- [`vp_prediction_table()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_prediction_table.md)
  : One row per feature and version, for predictions
- [`vp_rename()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_rename.md)
  : Rename features of a model
- [`vp_rename_candidates()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_rename_candidates.md)
  : Features that were probably renamed
- [`vp_ripple()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_ripple.md)
  : How many consequences each written change had
- [`vp_state_moves()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_state_moves.md)
  : Features that appeared, disappeared or changed status
- [`vp_top_movers()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_top_movers.md)
  : The features whose links changed most
- [`vp_version_distance()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_version_distance.md)
  : How far apart every two versions are

## Drawing

- [`vp_dot()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_dot.md)
  : The Graphviz (DOT) source of a drawing
- [`vp_dot_compare()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_dot_compare.md)
  : The Graphviz (DOT) source of a drawing of what changed
- [`vp_plot()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_plot.md)
  : Draw a model, some links or a feature tree
- [`vp_plot_compare()`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/vp_plot_compare.md)
  : Draw what changed between two versions

## The package

- [`variplex`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/variplex-package.md)
  [`variplex-package`](https://rheradio.github.io/variplex/reference/variplex-package.md)
  : variplex: analysis of strong dependency and conflict graphs of
  variability models
